subject: Econify — IP attribution, output ownership, and model-retrain permissions
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@econify.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify: output ownership & model retrain permissions

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement sent over a short questionnaire (attached) and flagged IP and training rights as the primary blockers for our legal team. Two quick asks for clarity before we escalate to legal:

1) Will Redwood assert any ownership over customer-generated output (responses produced by the model)?
2) Will Redwood use Econify inputs or outputs to further train or tune models without an explicit opt-in?

From our side, Econify needs explicit "no-training" language for customer content (including outputs) unless we sign a separate data-sharing agreement. If that's not your standard, can you outline the alternative paths (order form carveouts, Dedicated/Private deployment options, audit logs)?

Attached: Econify_Procurement_Questionnaire.pdf

Appreciate a short written note we can share with procurement/legal.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Platform Partnerships, Econify
michael@econify.com
+1 415-555-0193

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@econify.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: output ownership & model retrain permissions

Michael — thanks for the clear note and the questionnaire. Short answers up front:

- Output ownership: Customers retain ownership of the content they submit and the outputs generated. We do not claim title to customer outputs in our standard Order Form.

- Training / model retrain: By default (hosted API) Redwood has a limited feedback license that allows us to use telemetry and de-identified signals to improve our service, subject to privacy and export controls. However, we offer contractual carveouts: for Dedicated and Private deployments we can agree to a no-training carveout (i.e., Redwood will not use customer inputs or outputs to train or tune models). For hosted plans we can negotiate an explicit opt-out on the Order Form for large enterprise customers, usually paired with a minimum commitment or slightly different pricing.

I'll loop legal and propose a couple of redline options you can feed back to procurement. CC'ing Kimberly and Rishi to start drafting.

Action items:
- Kimberly: propose clean / redline language for Order Form and MSA options (no-training carveout; telemetry-only telemetry definition).
- Rishi: pricing path for Hosted opt-out vs Dedicated commitment.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Revenue, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
(415) 555-0102

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-09T15:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Econify — draft redlines for training/data use carveouts

Jonas / Rishi — following up with draft language and commentary. See redline attached (Redline_OrderForm_v1.pdf). High-level notes: 

1) Proposed clauses (clean language):
- "Customer Data" = customer inputs and derived outputs.
- "Feedback License" limited to anonymized telemetry (token-level metrics, aggregate failure rates) and expressly excludes content, prompt text, and generated outputs.
- Carveout option: "Customer may elect to exclude Customer Data from any Redwood model training or tuning activities; Redwood will not use, incorporate, or retain Customer Data for training in Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments when the carveout is selected and set forth in the Order Form."

2) Commercial trade-offs: hosted opt-out — acceptable only with a minimum 12-month commitment and a modest uplift to pricing to compensate for lost optimization signal. Dedicated/Private — standard inclusion in the enterprise Order Form.

3) Auditability & evidence: Econify asked for audit trails. We can deliver logging of feature flags and retention policy records; for hosted opt-outs we can provide monthly attestations and a high-level log export (subject to security review). If Econify needs detailed evidence, propose an advanced compliance package (add-on).

4) Next steps: legal to prepare a redline for the MSA/Order Form that includes both options (Hosted opt-out language + Dedicated/Private clause). I recommend we share the redline and a one-page summary for Econify procurement that lists the options and expected timelines.

Attaching: Redline_OrderForm_v1.pdf

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@econify.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-10T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Econify — IP attribution, output ownership, and model-retrain permissions

Michael — appreciate the urgency. Short commercial proposal to accelerate procurement: 

Option A (Hosted — faster onboarding):
- Redwood will agree in writing to a Feedback License limited to anonymized telemetry only (no prompts, no outputs used for model training).
- Requirement: 12-month minimum commitment; 15% price uplift on standard hosted T&Cs to offset lost optimization signal.
- Monthly high-level attestation log (contains flags that opt-out was applied).

Option B (Dedicated or Private — preferred for strict no-training):
- No-training carveout available by default for Dedicated and Private deployments; included in Order Form without price uplift.

If either option works, Kimberly will send final redline and we can route to signature. I can also share a quick addendum template that procurement can attach to the Order Form.

If you want a faster path to sign, I can confirm pricing and send an Order Form draft tomorrow.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Michael Grant <michael@econify.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@econify.com, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-10T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Econify — IP attribution, output ownership, and model-retrain permissions

Rishi / team — thanks for the clear options. Procurement feedback attached (Econify_Counter_Clean.docx). High-level counter positions: 

- Econify will not accept a price uplift for hosted to preserve an opt-out. Our preference is to keep hosted pricing neutral and instead accept a 6-month pilot with the opt-out in place; after pilot we can revisit.
- If Redwood cannot accept hosted-without-uplift, Econify is happy to move to Dedicated for production but needs a formal timeline for capacity and an implementation checklist.
- Econify requires the following minimum auditability: monthly attestations + a quarterly evidence package (redacted logs showing no data ingestion). We understand advanced compliance add-on may cost more; please include estimates.

Can Kimberly send a short draft (2–3 clauses) that captures the hosted pilot path + dedicated commitment path? Procurement needs the text to run through internal approvals.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Platform Partnerships, Econify

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@econify.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-14T08:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Econify — IP attribution, output ownership, and model-retrain permissions

Michael — thanks, good progress. Quick summary and recommended path so procurement/legal have a single ask to review: 

Agreed approach (two-track path):
1) Pilot (Hosted) — Econify pilot for 6 months with explicit hosted opt-out: Redwood will not use prompts or outputs for model training during the pilot. Redwood will provide monthly attestations and a quarterly redacted evidence package. No price uplift for pilot only. At the end of pilot, Econify may either: (a) accept Hosted (we would then require a 12-month commitment at the hosted opt-out price), or (b) move to Dedicated with the standard no-training carveout.

2) Dedicated (Production) — For production rollouts Redwood offers Dedicated capacity with a baked-in no-training carveout; pricing and lead time will be outlined in the Order Form. We will include an implementation checklist (networking, monitoring, capacity). Laura will scope Dedicated timings and capacity.

Next steps: 
- Kimberly: please prepare a short redline for the Order Form and a 1-page summary that captures the pilot language + Dedicated path. Put both documents in the Drive link and I will share the DocuSign template after Econify confirms the path.
- Laura: prepare an estimated Dedicated lead time & resource checklist (target delivery within 3 business days).
- Rishi: I will provide the hosted pilot Order Form draft and commercial terms to Michael by EOD tomorrow.
